circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
Skeletal remains were found on 2nd Avenue between 31st and 34th Street in an industrial area in Tampa, Florida on February 6, 1986.  It is estimated that she was found 3 to 8 weeks after her death. 
The anthropology report suggests that she had sustained injuries to the left side of her head and nose earlier in life which may have caused a deviated septum.  Her teeth were in poor condition and may have been causing her pain. 
Chemical  isotope analysis suggests  that she was likely born and raised in Florida.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: Body found floating near the Nine Mile Dam. It is not known how this man may have come to be in the river. The cause and Manner of death are both undetermined. The body was in an advanced state of decomposition. There was a skull fracture and other bodily injuries which were highly suspiscious for homicide and very possible to have occurred prior to the body entering into the water. This man had a possible tattoo "RICH" the R, C, and H were faily clear and possibly looked as if the letter "I" was present between the "R" and "C" as well but not definitively. The tattoo was not professional and was located on the left lateral bicep region.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
This body was found in a known hobo camp in the city of Spokane. Apparent transient. Several transients staying in the same area stated that they had known this man and that he had gone by the name of "Slow Harold". 

A clothing label had the name or work "KLENE" in permanent ink written on it. There were also 2 items of clothing that had what appear to be dry cleaning labels inside of them. The label shows a name of "Troy Linen Company" and a number of N-1805-75-1. We contacted several companies with similar or same company name and were unable to locate any useful records that might lead to an identification for this man.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
Died as the result of being struck by a tractor-trailer on the Interstate.
Personal Effects: Two cards and $30
Other Details: Decedent believed to be between 12 and 25 years old. Decedent was apparently a hitchhiker who may have used the first name "Donna" while traveling.  Subsequent investigation after her death revealed that she had been seen on the Florida coast during the days preceding her death.  In her pockets, she carried three business cards from; 1) Oklahoma City,OK  2)Canutillo, TX  3)West Monroe, LA.  Investigators contacted the names on the cards.  Two of the three were of no help.  The third was a Louisiana police officer who believed he had spoken to the girl several days before she was killed.  He recalled that he believed she was a runaway and had either a friend or sister in Las Vegas.  He believed he remembered a thick cajun accent.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
On December 26, 1983, the remains of the decedent  were discovered by hunters in a wooded area off of Interstate 95 . Based on forensic anthropological analysis of remains, the decedent is estimated to be a 4-6 year old female of mixed African American and European ancestry. Assuming the year of death was 1983, an individual aged 4-6 years at death would have been born between 1977 and 1979.

Isotope analysis indicates the decedent was likely born and lived in the USA. Oxygen isotopes indicate the decedent, and potentially her mother, may have migrated considerably around the Eastern U.S. during the short lifespan of the decedent. During pregnancy the mother possibly resided in the Midwest to Northeast U.S., then after birth the child spent the first years of her life in the northern portion of the Southeast U.S. Bone oxygen isotope data suggest that during the last couple years of her life, the child may have resided to the south of the region where she was found, in the areas of Central and Southern Florida and a region of Central Texas.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
On 10/24/1987 the skeletal remains of a Black female were found in an isolated rural area in Dickinson County, Kansas.

A Forensic Anthropologist determined that the victim was a Black female between the ages of 40 and 50 years old who was approximately 5’2 ½” to 5’5 ½” tall and it was estimated that she died sometime between 07/01/1987 and 09/15/1987.

The body was clad in a maroon T-shirt embossed on the front with the words “ASTRONAUT CROSS COUNTRY - We Believe In State Championships 1980”.  The body was wearing Jalapeno brand denim jeans and Sugar Babies brand tennis shoes.

The T-shirt worn by the victim was traced to the Titusville, Florida area as one High School in that area was called the Astronaut High School however no information has been developed from that area concerning missing persons fitting the description of the victim.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: On January 10, 1989, skeletal remains were found scattered over a wide area of desert near Barstow, CA (80 yards off Irwin Rd., 2.3 miles north of Highway 58).  Examination by a forensic anthropologist determines that the remains represent at least two persons: a male designated John Doe #02-89 (Coroner case #89-0443), and a female designated Jane Doe #04-89 (Coroner case #89-0444).  A mandible could not be verifiably associated with either, and was designated a separate unidentified remains: Undetermined Doe #01-89 (Coroner case #89-0180).  Thus far no DNA profile (STR or mtDNA) have been able to be obtained from either 89-0443 or 89-0444).  A mitochondrial profile has been developed from the mandible only (no STR).  Dental X-rays will be available for mandible only.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: The subject was a street person known as "The Box Lady."  Anthony Farrell has seen her many times on the street but never spoke to her until they met at a fast food restaurant.  He invited her to to eat and sleep at his residence, located at 720 Jones St.  They went to retrieve her shopping cart full of her possessions, and then walked back to his house.  She then decided to leave his premises but Mr. Farrell insisted that she take all of her belongings with her at which point she locked herself in Mr. Farrell's bathroom and remained there throughout the night despite Mr. Farrell's pleads to exit.  The next morning she Mr. Farrell found the bathroom unlocked and entered, but the subject was gone.  He saw the window was open and assumed she exited that way.  Later that day, Mr. Farrell looked out of his kitchen window and saw the subject lying unresponsive in the lightwell.  It appeared that the subject had tried to crawl from Mr. Farrell's bathroom window to the neighbors bedroom window and fell.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: Skeletal remains found buried in yard near this residence.  Believed to be Mr. Olaf Holt, 92 years old , a former resident of the residence who died (Natural?) in 1978 and his wife buried him someplace near the home.  Police never found him.  She later died and the new owner discovered the remains.  Mr. Holt has no family for a DNA source, no teeth for dental and no witnesses that knew him are still available.  Pathologist mentions remains having arthritic changes of an elderly man.  No missing persons has been found to match the skeletal remains.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: A death certificate was issued for James Laval Hurst on this case following investigation into a plane theft and crash in the Bahamas. Mr. Hurst was out on bond having been arrested for shooting another individual. Mr. Hurst's ex-wife paid for his plane fare to the Bahamas. Mr. Hurst and another man were reportedly (by an informant) taken to the airport runway in Marsh Harbor, Abacas, Bahamas where they stole a plane belonging to a man from West Palm Beach. The plane crashed shortly after take-off and was allegedly witnessed by the informant. The informant advised Naples Police Department and the bail bondsman who retrieved the remains from the crash and brought them to Naples where they were examined by the medical examiner and later by a forensic anthropologist. The anthropologist determined the co-mingled remains to be those of two males; one an approximately 50 year old white male and the other a younger individual around 20 years old. The passenger of the plane was believed to be a Colombian national. The Naples Police Department does not accept the presumptive identification and consider Mr. Hurst still at large.
A decomposed body was found under brush by a Forest Service Ranger.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
A citizen found a human skull at Tildon Park, marked the location found, and transported the skull to the Berkeley Police Department.  Berkeley PD contacted East Bay Regional Park Police Dept (EBRPPD) and EBRPPD determined skull was in their juristiction and took over the investigation (EBRPPD Case #81-2707).  EBRPPD contacted Contra Costa County Coroner to report the investigation (CC Coroner's Case #81-301).  
Through DNA testing, this case is related to Oakland PD homicide case #80-60910 (Alameda Coroner Case #80-1581, 07-28-1980).  Oakland PD's, Homicide Unit, is the lead investigative agency for this case.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:

notes.description:
Man presented himself as William Mooney/Moony, but that ID was never confirmed.  NO ID on decedent. Listed a SSN and DOB on application for Hospitality House, but were believed by CPD to be in error.  The SSN group number indicated the number was issued in Maryland.  UPDATE:  The SSN and DOB come back to a William Mooney/Moony, but also a couple aliases such as James Durm, Billy Thornsberry.  Has been in Arkansas and Joplin, MO.  As of March 2017 Fayetteville, AR and Joplin, MO PDs unable to locate Mooney/Durm

James Lee, 21 W. 9th St., Erie, PA as next of kin at Hospitality House. Unclear what happened with that follow up.  Also, the CPD talked with a Billy Mooney who worked for Ringling Brothers Circus.  Mooney refused to look at photo of decedent to ID as his father.  Not sure how that lead came about, but looking for old records.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: An unidentified deceased male was found on February 3, 1989 along Cobbs Creek Parkway, just south of Springfield Ave in Philadelphia, PA. The male had been deceased for approximately 2 days prior to being found. The investigation has revealed that the male was possibly from New York City and had the nickname "Dallas." The male is estimated to be 17-21 years old. He stood approximately 5’09" tall and weighed 139 pounds. He had black hair, medium length, styled in jheri curls. He had a tattoo on his upper right arm that appeared to be homemade. The tattoo is a heart with an arrow drawn through it and the initials "HB" separated on each side of the heart by the arrow. The male also had a gold tooth on one of his upper left teeth that would have been noticeable to others. He was found wearing a blue denim jacket with matching shirt and pants that had leather trim around the pockets. He also wore Travel Fox brand, blue sneakers and white socks with horizontal blue stripes.

A Georgia-Pacific West employee was conducting a routine check at the steam plant of a smoke problem in broiler #9 when he discovered skeletal remains laying on the broiler pipes.  The victim was likely a man of slight stature, about 20-40 years old.  He was 5’8” to 5’9” tall, weighing 130-155 pounds, wearing approximately a size 8 shoe.  He had decent dental work, with evidence of a root canal and gold and porcelain fillings.

notes.description:
Police found charred remnants of denim pants, a denim jacket, a lightweight shirt, and rubber-soled shoes.  Police also found a burned remnant of a Continental Airlines ticket, but there weren’t enough numbers to trace the ticket.  There were no keys, ID, wallet or anything to indicate he was a worker, and no workers were reported missing nor any abandoned vehicles located.

The pipes, which carried water heated by boiler exhaust, were 240 degrees. The air was 95 degrees, unless the boiler was running, when temperatures reached 370.  Officials estimated the victim had been in the chimney a few days to a few weeks. Records showed the boiler operated for 34 hours during September 17 and September 18, two days before the body was found, plus more hours the previous month.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery:
On May 1, 1982 a company was dredging the bottom of the Jordan River. They placed mud on the west bank as they progressed. Later while walking along the bank someone spotted what they thought was a rock on top of the dredged material. They went to pick up the rock and discovered it was a human skull, minus the mandible. Police responded and sifted the material, more bones  were discovered. The bones were determined to not be human bones.

The Medical Examiner took custody of the skull. They determined there was a bullet hole in the forehead with an exit in the back of the skull. The medical examiner believed the skull was very old.

circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: On 05/19/1984, two persons discovered the decedent floating face down in the water, approximately 2 to 3 feet from the south shoreline at Lake Calaveras in Carlsbad, CA.

clothingAndAccessoriesArticles.description: In the left rear pocket of the decedent's outer trousers was a billfold with the following printed inside on leather, "EL DIA 27 DE ABRIL DE 1984, CARLO GOMEZ S." Inside the wallet was a folded piece of paper with two addresses, possibly designating locations in Baja California, Mexico. There were also several names and telephone numbers written on the paper with area codes of 209, which is Madera County, Central CA, and one for a Victor Flores in Walla Walla, WA.

Hanging neatly on a tree limb at the campsite were two pairs of men's trousers, one inside the other" one Levi-type, "Gloria Vanderbilt", on the rear pocket and one dark blue pair of jeans. circumstances.description: Atlantic Ocean: 25-40 miles from Anguila Key, Bahama Banks
circumstances.circumstancesOfRecovery: September 8, 1980 a US Coast Guard Aircraft observed five bodies floating in the ocean near a submerged sunken vessel on the east side of Santaren Channel. The bodies were floating in water 25-40 miles from Anguilla Key, Bahama Banks. Upon Coast Guard arrival on scene, they retrieved all 5 bodies including a sixth body. There was no personal property or debris in the water. The sunken vessel was a wooden 2 masted sail ship, approximately 25-35 feet in length. All bodies were an advanced state of decomposition. While at the scene, another boat with 25-30 people on board approached the Coast Guard cutter and were taken aboard (alive and well) and transported to Dodge Island.
